items.note: Carwow article dated 13 May 2021. States the Supreme Court rejected Ecologistas en Acción's appeal against the July 2019 TSJM ruling annulling ordinance articles 21-25 (the legal basis of Madrid Central); says that until the ruling is final (expected the following July) Madrid Central stays in force and keeps fining; says the PP-led city government is expected to announce its own Madrid 360 plan. 'Planned to replace' is a fair reading of an expected announcement. The visible H1 is 'Así queda Madrid Central tras su anulación'; the draft source_title is the HTML title tag without the site name, which is acceptable.

eldiario.es, 17 Nov 2021: Más Madrid filed a contencioso-administrativo appeal at the TSJM against article 23 of the Sustainable Mobility Ordinance approved in September 2021 (replacing Madrid Central with a low-emission zone); Vox also appealed the same day at the TSJM. The 2025 tariff decree (BOCM 13 Dec 2024) cites the ordinance as modified by the agreement of 13 September 2021 (BOCM 21 Sept 2021). Note: Más Madrid's appeal targets article 23 only; the draft does not say otherwise. Title matches the page H1.

Autonoción page published 26.01.2022: NO2 above 60 micrograms per cubic metre (urban background stations, previous day) raises SER tariff 60 percent; above 70 raises it 100 percent (also in a declared mobility-restriction scenario); zero-emission vehicles exempt; ECO label gets a bonus of up to 75 percent. Title matches the H1.

Motor.es page is published 17/09/2024 17:30 but does not give the date of the ruling; the 17 September date is the article's publication date. Supported: TSJM (Sección Segunda, Sala Contencioso-Administrativo) annulled the parts of the Sustainable Mobility Ordinance defining the scope of the low-emission zone covering the whole municipality, after a Vox challenge; reasoning was insufficient prior reports, especially economic; ruling not yet final and open to a cassation appeal by the city. The later Motor.es piece (22 Apr 2026) only says 'September 2024'.
items.corrected_text: A report published on 17 September 2024 says the regional high court (TSJM) annulled the parts of the Sustainable Mobility Ordinance that defined the scope of the citywide low-emission zone, after a challenge by Vox, because the prior reports, especially the economic one, were insufficient. The ruling was not yet final and the city could still file a cassation appeal.

items.note: Page published 22/04/2026. Supported: the Supreme Court refused to take up the city's appeal (it declined to admit/study it, order is final, costs of 2,000 euros), leaving the September 2024 TSJM annulment in place; the annulled rules had already been replaced by a newer ordinance (the page dates that ordinance to March 2025, which does not match the 2026 ordinance elsewhere in the draft, so the date is best left out). NOT supported: 'In July 2026 Vox asked the TSJM to enforce the ruling and require refunds'. The page says only that Vox announced a motion for the 29 April municipal plenary asking the mayor to refund the fines. 'Rejected the appeal' is looser than 'declined to hear it'.
items.corrected_text: A report of 22 April 2026 says the Supreme Court refused to admit the city's appeal against the September 2024 TSJM annulment, leaving that ruling final, and that the annulled rules had already been replaced by a newer ordinance. The report adds that Vox announced a motion for the 29 April municipal plenary asking the mayor to refund low-emission-zone fines.

items.note: BOCM nº 107, 7 May 2026, p.222: corrects material errors in Ordinance 2/2026 of 24 March 2026 (amending the Sustainable Mobility Ordinance on special-protection low-emission zones and the SER), approved by the Pleno on 24 March 2026, and computer-editing errors in the text published in BOAM nº 10.103 of 10 April 2026. The corrections are typographic/wording fixes in the preamble and text (e.g. misplaced quotation marks, 'por mediante'); nothing substantive is stated on the page in the part read. Draft source_title is truncated and has '(BOCM nº 107)' appended; real title below. Date is the plenary approval date.
items.corrected_title: Corrección de los errores materiales advertidos en el texto de la Ordenanza 2/2026, de 24 de marzo, por la que se modifica la Ordenanza de Movilidad Sostenible, de 5 de octubre de 2018, en materia de zonas de bajas emisiones de especial protección y del servicio de estacionamiento regulado y de los errores materiales de edición informática advertidos en el texto publicado de la ordenanza en el BOAM n.º 10.103, de 10 de abril de 2026

items.note: eldiario.es/Somos Madrid, 11 Dec 2025. Supported: up to 22 new neighbourhoods; gradual; first phase by end of 2029 (neighbourhoods already foreseen in the 2021 ordinance) adds 11,372 spaces; Puente de Vallecas and Moratalaz reached for the first time; extended hours beyond 21:00 weekdays, from 15:00 Saturdays, and Sundays/holidays in high-intensity zones. Overstated/ambiguous: the 66,120 figure is the second phase (to end of 2035) ADDING 66,120 spaces (36 percent on a base of 181,493), not a cumulative total by 2035; the draft wording 'up to 66,120 by 2035' can be read as cumulative. The page says the Junta de Gobierno was to give initial approval that Thursday, so 'before approval' is fair.
items.corrected_text: A report of 11 December 2025 says a draft change to the Sustainable Mobility Ordinance, due for initial approval by the city government that day, would let regulated on-street parking (SER) spread in phases to up to 22 more neighbourhoods: about 11,372 spaces by the end of 2029, then a second phase to 2035 adding 66,120 spaces, reaching Puente de Vallecas and Moratalaz for the first time. It would also allow extended SER hours beyond 21:00 on weekdays, from 15:00 on Saturdays and on Sundays and holidays in high-demand zones.

items.note: BOCM nº 297, 13 Dec 2024, Decree of 2 Dec 2024, dispositivo Cuarto: EMT-managed park-and-ride spaces are free if the car is parked at least 5 and at most 16 hours and public transport is used during the stay; otherwise general rotational use and the general maximum tariff apply. Effective 1 Jan 2025. Draft source_title uses an ellipsis and '(BOCM nº 297)'; real title given.
items.corrected_title: Decreto de 2 de diciembre de 2024 del delegado del Área de Gobierno de Urbanismo, Medio Ambiente y Movilidad, por el que se aprueban para el año 2025 las tarifas de las plazas rotacionales de los aparcamientos municipales mixtos y de rotación de la ciudad de Madrid en gestión directa e indirecta

items.note: CRTM press release 23/10/2020: the Consortium is finalising agreements to add 19 more car parks to the Aparca+T pilot network; says signature of an agreement with the Madrid city council for three EMT-operated car parks (Wanda Metropolitano, Nuestra Señora del Recuerdo, Avenida de Portugal) is very advanced. The 'plan, not completed' caveat is correct. Title matches page H1.

Decree dispositivo Primero: 2025 maximum car tariffs 0.0496 / 0.0448 / 0.0594 euros per minute (0-30, 31-90, 91-660 min), 38.00 euros from 661 minutes up to 24 hours, VAT included; applies to both direct and indirect (concession) management; fundamento Cuarto cites regional CPI change of 1.5 percent Sept 2023 to Sept 2024. NOT on the page: the 2024 decree figures (0.0489, 0.0441, 0.0585, 37.45); the page does not mention 2024 tariffs at all, so those must be removed.
items.corrected_text: The decree sets 2025 maximum rotational tariffs for cars, VAT included, in both directly managed (EMT) and concession car parks: 0.0496 euros per minute for 0-30 minutes, 0.0448 for 31-90 and 0.0594 for 91-660 minutes, and 38.00 euros for 661 minutes up to 24 hours. It cites a 1.5 percent change in the regional consumer price index between September 2023 and September 2024.
items.corrected_title: Decreto de 2 de diciembre de 2024 del delegado del Área de Gobierno de Urbanismo, Medio Ambiente y Movilidad, por el que se aprueban para el año 2025 las tarifas de las plazas rotacionales de los aparcamientos municipales mixtos y de rotación de la ciudad de Madrid en gestión directa e indirecta

items.note: Dispositivo Séptimo: high-demand tariff in direct or indirect rotation car parks less than 400 m from a facility able to hold more than 5,000 people during a high-attendance event, from one hour before the event, 30 percent above the generic tariff for the first four hours; 15 percent reduction for vehicles with three or more occupants. Dispositivo Octavo: effective 1 Jan 2025 'sin perjuicio' of the last paragraph of Séptimo, which makes applying the high-demand tariff and the occupancy bonus conditional on the car park operator having technology to verify real vehicle occupancy (both applied together). The draft omits that condition and calls it an addition ('adds'), which the page does not state explicitly.
items.corrected_text: The decree, effective 1 January 2025, sets a high-demand tariff 30 percent above the generic one for the first four hours at rotation car parks less than 400 metres from venues able to hold over 5,000 people during large events, starting one hour before the event, with a 15 percent reduction for vehicles with three or more occupants. Applying the tariff and the reduction requires the car park operator to have technology to verify actual occupancy.
items.corrected_title: Decreto de 2 de diciembre de 2024 del delegado del Área de Gobierno de Urbanismo, Medio Ambiente y Movilidad, por el que se aprueban para el año 2025 las tarifas de las plazas rotacionales de los aparcamientos municipales mixtos y de rotación de la ciudad de Madrid en gestión directa e indirecta

items.note: Decree preamble: car park service provided via concessionaires (indirect management) and via direct management by EMT, a company with fully municipal capital; dispositivo Sexto: EMT may apply tariffs taking vehicles' environmental classification into account in directly managed rotation spaces (art. 123.1.a of the ordinance).
items.corrected_title: Decreto de 2 de diciembre de 2024 del delegado del Área de Gobierno de Urbanismo, Medio Ambiente y Movilidad, por el que se aprueban para el año 2025 las tarifas de las plazas rotacionales de los aparcamientos municipales mixtos y de rotación de la ciudad de Madrid en gestión directa e indirecta

items.note: Somos Madrid, 27 July 2023. The city government approved the TENDER (licitación) for management of the three Velázquez car parks (Ayala, Jorge Juan, Juan Bravo) for 25 years, with residents' use rights respected until 1 June 2048; it was not an approved/awarded concession with an operator yet. Other figures check out: 1,894 spaces, of which 622 for residents (1,272 rotation); 128 spaces reserved for electric recharging (not '128 charge points'); concessionaire must spend about 17.2 million euros on modernisation. Headline says 'privatiza hasta el 2048'.
items.corrected_text: On 27 July 2023 the city government approved the tender for a roughly 25-year concession for three Calle Velázquez car parks (Ayala, Jorge Juan, Juan Bravo), with residents' use rights respected until 1 June 2048. The report gives 1,894 spaces, including 622 for residents and 128 reserved for electric charging, and says the concessionaire must spend about 17.2 million euros on modernisation.

items.note: Vivir Ediciones, 25 March 2026 (15:31): EMT Madrid's 2025 accounts show parking income ('ingresos por aparcamientos') of 19.2 million euros, total income 887.3 million, profit 3.26 million. Title matches the H1.

Movilidad Eléctrica, 14 Feb 2024 (H1 matches draft title; the HTML title tag is 'Localizamos 14 nuevos puntos de recarga en Madrid'). Supported: four EMT car parks upgraded (Pedro Zerolo, Plaza Mayor, Olavide, Almagro) with 2+4+2+6 = 14 new chargers. Not supported: '33 more chargers across ten further car parks'. The page says the municipal plans cover installing 33 new chargers in ten car parks (Almagro, Benavente, Fuencarral, Marqués de Salamanca, Montalbán, Plaza Mayor, Olavide, Pedro Zerolo, San Epifanio, Villa de París), which includes the four already done, so they are not 'further' or additional; funding is Next Generation EU.
items.corrected_text: A report of 14 February 2024 says EMT had completed upgrades at four public car parks (Pedro Zerolo, Plaza Mayor, Olavide and Almagro) that added 14 charge points in total. It adds that municipal plans cover 33 new chargers across ten car parks, including those four, funded by EU Next Generation money.

items.note: electrive.com (Spanish), 28.06.2020, updated 29 June 2020. Direct fetch is blocked by Cloudflare; read via an archived copy and WebFetch. Page: 45 publicly accessible fast-charging points in Madrid (31 on public land, 14 on private property); EMT and i-DE signed an agreement to advise on bus electrification and to install EV charge points in car parks and public spaces managed by EMT. The agreement date is not given, 'mid-2020' reflects the article date. Title matches.

Page is the national portal datos.gob.es (publisher Ayuntamiento de Madrid), not the city's own catalogue. Dataset 'EMT. Aparcamientos EMT' description matches (municipal car parks under EMT integral management; types rotation, residents, mixed, park-and-ride; location and characteristics). There is no 'last modified' field: dataset creation date is 2025-11-04 and the file distributions (GeoJSON/CSV/KML/ZIP/PDF) are dated 2026-02-14. 'Last modified in February 2026' therefore overstates what is stated; refresh rate is listed as unknown.
items.corrected_text: The national open data catalogue datos.gob.es lists an Ayuntamiento de Madrid dataset, 'EMT. Aparcamientos EMT', describing the location and characteristics of EMT-run municipal car parks (rotation, resident, mixed and park-and-ride); the dataset was created on 4 November 2025 and its file distributions are dated 14 February 2026.

items.note: datos.madrid.es tag listing: 'EMT. Plazas totales y disponibles por hora en aparcamientos por mes y año' (CSV, update frequency Diaria, published 3 Nov 2025); 'Estudio de satisfacción de clientes de plazas de aparcamientos gestionadas por la EMT' shows update date 24 July 2026. The draft source_title is a descriptor, not a real title. The page's own title is 'Conjunto de datos - Portal de datos abiertos del Ayuntamiento de Madrid' (a keyword-filtered listing, tag 'emt').
items.corrected_title: Conjunto de datos - Portal de datos abiertos del Ayuntamiento de Madrid (listing filtered by keyword 'emt')

items.note: comunidad.madrid press page published 16 Jan 2026: record 736,874,012 Metro de Madrid users/trips in 2025 (headline says 'usuarios'; body says 'viajes'), up 3 percent on 715,208,882 in 2024, despite partial Line 6 closures. Busiest day in the company's history was 28 Nov (Black Friday) with 2,819,020 trips, BUT the page explicitly excludes 12 March 2004 (demonstration after the 11-M attacks). The draft's 'busiest day ever' omits that exclusion. Figures are for the Metro de Madrid network (regional), not Madrid city only. Title matches the og:title; date 2025 is the data year.
items.corrected_text: The Community of Madrid reported on 16 January 2026 a record 736,874,012 Metro de Madrid trips in 2025, 3 percent above the 715,208,882 of 2024. It says the busiest day in the company's history, excluding 12 March 2004, was 28 November (Black Friday) with 2,819,020 trips.

items.note: BOCM nº 311, 31 Dec 2025, p.65: the CRTM board on 29 Dec 2025 approved keeping 2026 public transport prices at those of the second half of 2025; context is Real Decreto-Ley 17/2025 of 23 Dec providing aid: free child passes, 50 percent off youth passes, 20 percent off other multi-trip passes. The page adds the Consortium plans to keep regional/municipal co-funding so users' prices stay the same. Draft source_title uses an ellipsis and '(BOCM nº 311)'; real title given.
items.corrected_title: RESOLUCIÓN de 29 de diciembre de 2025, de la Dirección-Gerencia del Consorcio Regional de Transportes Públicos Regulares de Madrid, por la que se dispone la publicación del acuerdo del Consejo de Administración por el que se determinan los precios del transporte público en el año 2026

items.note: Tourism yearbook PDF (88 pages, created 29 May 2026), foreword and 'Principales datos': record international tourist spending 17,896 million euros in 2025 (71 percent above 2019, 11.1 percent above 2024); more than 11 million visitors (total 11,236,564 domestic plus international, not only international); 'durante nueve meses ... supera los 900.000 visitantes mensuales'. The 11 million figure is total visitors, while the 17.9 billion is international only; the draft wording is compatible. Minor: p.14 of the PDF prints 17.986 million instead of 17.896, an internal typo. Cover title is 'Madrid 2025 ANUARIO TURISMO' (running header 'Anuario de turismo Madrid 2025'); '(Madrid Destino)' is not in the title, the document is credited to Turismo del Ayuntamiento de Madrid. Date should be the data year, not the publication month.

corrected_summary: Madrid's municipal rotation car parks are run partly through concessionaires and partly directly by EMT, and the city approves maximum rotational tariffs each year by decree, updated by regional consumer prices. The regional high court annulled the parts of the mobility ordinance defining the citywide low-emission zone in September 2024, the Supreme Court declined to admit the city's appeal in April 2026, and the city council approved a further ordinance modification (Ordinance 2/2026) on 24 March 2026. Metro de Madrid recorded 736.9 million trips in 2025, and the regional transport consortium kept 2026 public transport prices at their second-half 2025 level.
